name: Carysil (earlier Acrysil) Ltd
tagline: Global B2B quartz/stainless-steel kitchen-sink and appliances manufacturer riding a genuine China+1 sourcing shift - sole or dominant supplier to Karran (US), GROHE and IKEA plus a broadening Home Depot/Lowe's/Howdens/Amazon US customer base - with accelerating growth, sustained margin expansion and active deleveraging, but a full ~31x trailing P/E and management's own 15% growth guide still don't support a literal 10x/100x return case at the current ~Rs 3,000-3,050 Cr market cap
business_overview: Carysil (renamed from Acrysil) manufactures quartz composite and stainless-steel kitchen sinks plus kitchen appliances/faucets, selling B2B to global brands and distributors across UK, US, India (fast-growing domestic push) and EU. It is the sole quartz-sink supplier to Karran USA (a 150,000-unit/year long-term agreement) and to GROHE, supplies IKEA globally (targeting 70-75% of IKEA's non-US quartz sink sourcing, up from ~25%), and has an extended Home Depot partnership plus newer Lowe's, Howdens UK, Hafele and Amazon USA relationships disclosed in the Q1 FY27 commentary - a materially broader customer base than the Karran/GROHE/IKEA framing alone suggested. Building capacity across all four product lines simultaneously (quartz sinks, stainless-steel sinks, kitchen appliances, faucets) funded largely internally while also actively deleveraging (net D/E ~33% FY26, finance cost -15.8% YoY, target debt-free by 2030).
fundamentals_table: ROE ~17% (3-yr avg FY24-26); ROCE 18% FY26 (dipped to 15% FY25, recovered)
FY26 full year +13.2% YoY (Rs 924 Cr); Q1 FY27 +16.5% YoY (Rs 264.8 Cr) - accelerating; guidance 15% for FY27
FY26 full year EBITDA margin 19.9% (+256bps YoY); Q1 FY27 21.2% (+175bps YoY) - tracking/beating upper band of 18-20% FY27 guidance
FY26 full year PAT (after MI) +54% YoY to Rs 98.2 Cr; Q1 FY27 +37.7% YoY - operating leverage sustained across a full year, not one quarter
Net D/E ~33% FY26; finance cost down 15.8% YoY (Rs 23.4 Cr -> Rs 19.7 Cr) as debt is repaid; target debt-free by 2030
P/E ~30.7x trailing (TTM EPS Rs 37.55) - full, not cheap, for 15% guided growth
fundamentals_narrative: A structurally improving story that has now held for a full fiscal year, not just a quarter: FY26 revenue grew 13.2% to Rs 924 Cr while EBITDA margin expanded 256bps to 19.9% and PAT (after MI) surged 54% to Rs 98.2 Cr; Q1 FY27 extended the trend (revenue +16.5%, margin 21.2%, ahead of the 18-20% FY27 guide). Utilisation is running hot (SS sinks 94%, quartz 80% in Q1 FY27 - management describes the factory as 'under stress'), which is both the near-term margin driver and the reason for the ~Rs 80-90 Cr/year capex program expanding quartz capacity from 1.0m to 1.25m units/annum by end FY27. Unusually, growth capex and deleveraging are happening together: net D/E fell to ~33% and finance costs dropped 15.8% YoY even as capex continued, funded mostly via internal accruals. The customer base has also broadened materially beyond the original Karran/GROHE/IKEA framing - an extended Home Depot partnership plus new Lowe's, Howdens UK, Hafele and Amazon USA relationships were disclosed in Q1 FY27, tempering (not eliminating) the community's customer-concentration concern. The one lingering caution, not re-verified with fresh filings this pass: 60+ day receivables/working-capital days flagged by a community member (Feb 2025) as more contract-manufacturer-like than the 'sole supplier' framing implies. Screener's 10-year table shows a genuinely strong Coffee-Can track record (8 of 11 fiscal years cleared both >=10% revenue growth and >=15% ROCE), with the only misses (FY17, FY18, FY20) forming one identifiable soft patch, not chronic inconsistency.
